def: An n-dimensional array with a shape, a number format (dtype) and a device, which can also record the operations applied to it.
PyTorch's automatic differentiation: it records operations as code runs and applies the chain rule backwards to produce gradients.
The record of operations and their inputs built during the forward pass, which backward() walks in reverse.
Building the computation graph as ordinary code executes, so that control flow in Python changes the graph with no special syntax.
Differentiating by one backward sweep over the graph, giving the gradient with respect to every input at a small multiple of the forward cost.
The behaviour that each backward pass adds to the existing .grad values rather than replacing them, so they must be cleared every step.
An object that owns parameters and sub-modules and defines a forward method, so a whole network can be treated as one callable.
A plain dictionary from parameter names to tensors, used to save and restore a model.
An object that holds the parameters and turns their gradients into updates when step() is called.
A small slice of the training set used for one gradient estimate and one parameter update.
One full pass over the training set.
The raw, unnormalised scores a classifier outputs before softmax turns them into probabilities.
Queuing GPU work and returning at once, so that Python runs ahead while the GPU computes.
